name: Balancer V1
rootCause: joinswapPoolAmountOut rounding drain across 5 pools. Lost: ~$110,839 for this DPI/USDC/WETH/WBTC pool (~$234K aggregate across all 5 vulnerable pools)

descriptions.text: joinswapPoolAmountOut rounding drain across 5 pools. Lost: ~$110,839 for this DPI/USDC/WETH/WBTC pool (~$234K aggregate across all 5 vulnerable pools)

An attacker exploited a rounding/precision vulnerability in legacy Balancer V1 contracts. Using flash loans to compress WBTC reserves to near-zero, they minted a large amount of BPT with only 1 satoshi of WBTC and then proportionally exited to drain DPI, USDC, WETH and WBTC from the pool.

On August 30, 2026, an attacker exploited a rounding error in Balancer V1's join logic on Ethereum Mainnet, draining approximately $234,000 from five legacy pools by compressing WBTC reserves to near-zero and minting pool tokens for negligible input. The bug resulted from single-asset join math that incorrectly rounded in the user's favor when pool balances became very small. Balancer V1's joinswapPoolAmountOut function allowed a user to specify pool-token output, and calculated the required token input using fixed-point math. When the pool's WBTC balance was reduced to near zero, the calculation rounded down, letting the attacker mint large amounts of BPT with a one-satoshi input.…
